sentences.text: The Crime and Corruption Commission analysed Queensland Police Service corruption risks using complaints, investigations, intelligence and public information from July 2020 to June 2025.
sentences.support:
complaints received by the CCC relating to the Queensland Police Service between 1 July 2020 
and 30 June 2025

sentences.text: Its analysis includes both corrupt conduct and police misconduct, with risks varying between operational policing and corporate or administrative work.
sentences.support: references to “corruption” include both corrupt conduct and police misconduct.

sentences.text: The CCC identified incident responses, offence investigations and confidential information management as high-risk activities, while noting that most complaints were referred to the police service.
sentences.support:
Responding to incidents, investigating offences and managing confidential information are 
high-risk activities for the sector.

sentences.text: The CCC outlined prevention measures including employee screening, ongoing training, supervision, information controls and audits of policing and corporate activities.
sentences.support: Robust employee and recruit screening, supported by initial and ongoing training and education

findings.quote:
Responding to incidents, investigating offences and managing confidential information are 
high-risk activities for the sector.
Corruption risks vary based on role and level of interaction with the community.

notes: Complaints are allegations, not established misconduct. Prevention strategies are unnumbered; no formal recommendation count is asserted.
